evals.name: intermittent-fasting-pl-cs
evals.prompt: Порівняй зростання інтересу до інтервального голодування в польськомовній та чеськомовній Wikipedia за останні два роки.
evals.expected_output: Ukrainian answer + one-page PDF. Czech article exists, Polish Wikipedia has no linked article (content gap, or a clearly labelled proxy). Growth reported with uncertainty and confidence; period stated; relative vs raw distinction explained.
assertions: report.pdf exists in outputs and has exactly 1 page
response.md is written in Ukrainian
Response states the analysed period (months or dates)
Every growth/decline claim carries an uncertainty measure (interval or explicit confidence level)
Response names the Wikipedia articles (or article basket/proxies) that were measured
Response says Polish Wikipedia has no dedicated article on intermittent fasting, or clearly labels any Polish page used as a proxy
Czech interest is reported as declining (ground truth: relative -34% [-53%, -5%], MEDIUM confidence; raw views -42%; 2025-09..2026-08 vs previous 12 months)
Response distinguishes relative interest (share of all wiki views) from raw views, or mentions the Wikipedia-wide traffic decline
Does not name countries in place of language editions as the audiences (e.g. 'Vietnam', 'Turkey', 'Poland') unless it cites the reader-country data
Does not subtract the whole-wiki change from relative growth or compare the two as if relative growth still contained it (no double counting)

evals.name: astronomy-uk-trust
evals.prompt: Ми думаємо додати курс з астрономії до освітнього застосунку. Чи зростає інтерес до цієї теми в україномовній Wikipedia, і наскільки цьому зростанню можна довіряти?
evals.expected_output: Ukrainian answer + one-page PDF. Interest in astronomy articles in uk.wikipedia is declining (not growing), relative to the whole wiki too; explicit trust assessment (interval, consistency, confidence grade) and caveats (seasonality, bot-detection change, proxy articles).
assertions: report.pdf exists in outputs and has exactly 1 page
response.md is written in Ukrainian
Response states the analysed period (months or dates)
Every growth/decline claim carries an uncertainty measure (interval or explicit confidence level)
Response names the Wikipedia articles (or article basket/proxies) that were measured

Response concludes that interest in astronomy on Ukrainian Wikipedia is NOT growing (ground truth: declining; 7-article basket relative about -33% [-44%, -20%], HIGH; core article 'Астрономія' alone also declines)
Response gives an explicit trust assessment backed by evidence (interval, month-by-month consistency, or confidence grade)
Response mentions at least one data caveat: seasonality, the 2025 bot-detection change, or that articles are only proxies
Does not name countries in place of language editions as the audiences (e.g. 'Vietnam', 'Turkey', 'Poland') unless it cites the reader-country data
Does not subtract the whole-wiki change from relative growth or compare the two as if relative growth still contained it (no double counting)

evals.name: english-learning-audiences
evals.prompt: Ми створюємо застосунок для вивчення мов. Порівняй інтерес до вивчення англійської у вибраних нами мовних розділах Wikipedia — польському, турецькому, іспанському, в'єтнамському та німецькому — і підготуй короткий звіт: які аудиторії варто дослідити наступними й чому?
evals.expected_output: Ukrainian answer + one-page PDF ranking the five language audiences using size, growth and confidence, with reasons, proxy articles named, and caveats (language is not country, curiosity is not purchase intent).
assertions: report.pdf exists in outputs and has exactly 1 page
response.md is written in Ukrainian
Response states the analysed period (months or dates)
Every growth/decline claim carries an uncertainty measure (interval or explicit confidence level)
Response names the Wikipedia articles (or article basket/proxies) that were measured
Response ranks or prioritises the five language audiences explicitly
Ranking reasons use both audience size and growth (or intensity), not just one number
Response mentions that a language edition is not the same as a country (or gives a reader-geography caveat)
Response notes that Wikipedia interest is not purchase intent or recommends validating with another signal
Does not describe a change whose 95% interval crosses zero as growth or a positive trend (e.g. 'English language · vi +2% [-21%, +31%]' is 'no clear change')
Reasons are grounded in the data: no unsupported outside claims (competition, market size, demographics) or misreadings of the metrics presented as findings
Does not name countries in place of language editions as the audiences (e.g. 'Vietnam', 'Turkey', 'Poland') unless it cites the reader-country data
Does not subtract the whole-wiki change from relative growth or compare the two as if relative growth still contained it (no double counting)
Contains no invented market facts presented as findings (market shares, numbers of speakers, revenue, 'users pay') that are not in the tool output

evals.name: followup-add-languages
evals.prompt:
[Контекст розмови: раніше ти вже проаналізував інтерес до вивчення англійської у польському, турецькому, іспанському, в'єтнамському та німецькому розділах Wikipedia; твої попередні результати, відповідь і звіт лежать у папці <previous analysis folder>]

evals.expected_output: Re-run with pt and uk added, same IELTS/TOEFL basket, weights favouring growth, updated one-page PDF, and an explanation of what changed.
assertions: report.pdf exists in outputs and has exactly 1 page
response.md is written in Ukrainian
The updated analysis covers all seven language editions (pl, tr, es, vi, de, pt, uk)
Measurement stays consistent with the previous analysis (same articles/basket), or the response explains what changed and why
The new ranking explicitly gives growth more weight than audience size, and the response says so
Growth figures for the new languages carry an uncertainty measure (interval or confidence level)
Response states how the recommendation or ranking changed compared with the previous version
Does not describe a change whose 95% interval crosses zero as growth or a positive trend (e.g. '+2% [-21%, +31%]' is 'no clear change')
Reasons are grounded in the data: no unsupported outside claims (competition, market size, demographics) or misreadings of the metrics presented as findings
Does not name countries in place of language editions as the audiences (e.g. 'Vietnam', 'Turkey', 'Poland') unless it cites the reader-country data
Does not subtract the whole-wiki change from relative growth or compare the two as if relative growth still contained it (no double counting)
Contains no invented market facts presented as findings (market shares, numbers of speakers, revenue, 'users pay') that are not in the tool output
Does not recommend avoiding an audience because the App Store search returned no (relevant) apps

evals.name: growing-subtopics-astronomy
evals.prompt: У нас освітній застосунок з астрономії для українських школярів. Які підтеми астрономії зараз набирають інтерес в україномовній Вікіпедії, і з чого варто почати новий модуль?
evals.expected_output: Uses expand/discover to find sub-topics automatically, lists growing vs declining sub-topics with intervals and confidence, notes school seasonality, recommends a module grounded in the data.
assertions: response.md is written in Ukrainian
Sub-topics were found with the skill's automatic tools (expand or discover output exists), not only a hand-picked list
Lists at least 3 sub-topics with a growth estimate and an interval or confidence level
Does not call a sub-topic growing when its 95% interval crosses zero
Mentions a seasonality/school-year pattern or a data caveat (bot-detection update, low volume)
Recommends a concrete starting module and ties the reason to numbers from the output

evals.name: fasting-season-forecast-signals
evals.prompt: Плануємо запуск застосунку про інтервальне голодування в Чехії та Німеччині. Коли в році пік інтересу, чого чекати в наступні 12 місяців, і чи підтверджують це дані Google?
evals.expected_output: Analyze cs and de (36 months), report seasonal peaks, 12-month forecast with 80% range, run signals (Google Trends agreement + App Store), one-page PDF.
assertions: report.pdf exists in outputs and has exactly 1 page
response.md is written in Ukrainian
States the seasonal peak month(s) for each of the two languages/countries from the tool output
Gives a 12-month forecast as a range (80% interval), not a single number, with a caveat that it is a scenario
Reports the Google Trends result for CZ and DE and whether it agrees with Wikipedia (or clearly states it was unavailable)
Includes App Store competition context for at least one country
The PDF includes the Second signals section (signals were run before report)

evals.name: whats-growing-polish-wiki
evals.prompt: Що зараз найбільше набирає інтерес у польськомовній Вікіпедії, окрім новин про знаменитостей? Шукаємо ідеї для контенту.
evals.expected_output: Runs discover pl, lists growing topics with confidence, flags news-driven transient items, suggests follow-up analysis.
assertions: response.md is written in Ukrainian
Used the discover command on pl (discover output exists)
Lists at least 5 growing topics with growth and confidence
No person/celebrity pages among the recommended topics
Flags that event/news-driven items (tournaments, eclipses) are likely transient or treats LOW confidence rows as hypotheses
Suggests a concrete next step (e.g. analyze a shortlisted topic, check a second signal)
